title: If God to Build the House Deny
description: If God to Build the House Deny in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 127, part 2, headed “God all in all”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: If God to build the house de-ny, The buil-ders work in vain; And towns, with-out his wake-ful eye, An use-less watch main-tain.

lines: If God to build the house deny,
And towns, without his wakeful eye,
And till the stars ascend the skies
Short be your sleep, and coarse your fare;
In vain, till God has blest;
But if his smiles attend your care,
You shall have food and rest.
Nor all the earthly joys he sends,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
